description: AWS CDK (TypeScript) infrastructure for one-command deploy (cdk deploy): DynamoDB table, Lambda functions (bundled via NodejsFunction/esbuild) wired to API Gateway HTTP API with CORS, Bedrock InvokeModel IAM permissions, and S3 + CloudFront static hosting for the frontend with a deploy of the built assets. Plus a comprehensive README deploy guide. Depends on FEAT-002 (backend handlers) and FEAT-003 (frontend build output).
steps: Create infra/package.json (name @ddm/infra, deps: aws-cdk-lib, constructs; devDeps: aws-cdk, typescript, @types/node, ts-node; scripts: build=tsc, synth='cdk synth', deploy='cdk deploy', bootstrap='cdk bootstrap').
Create infra/cdk.json with app 'npx ts-node --prefer-ts-exts bin/app.ts' and sensible context.
Create infra/bin/app.ts instantiating the stack, reading region/account from env (CDK_DEFAULT_*).

Create infra/lib/digital-monster-stack.ts: (a) DynamoDB Table 'Monsters' with partition key id (string), PAY_PER_REQUEST, removalPolicy configurable; (b) three/four NodejsFunction Lambdas (getMonster, saveMonster, chat, battle) pointing at packages/backend/src/handlers/*.ts with bundling, env TABLE_NAME, ALLOWED_ORIGIN and optional BEDROCK_MODEL_* overrides; grant table read/write; grant chat+battle lambda bedrock:InvokeModel on Claude model ARNs (use a broad bedrock:InvokeModel resource with foundation-model ARNs for haiku/sonnet/opus, region-parameterized); (c) HTTP API (apigatewayv2) with routes GET /monster, POST /monster, POST /chat, POST /battle integrated to the lambdas, CORS enabled; (d) S3 bucket (private) + CloudFront distribution with OAC serving the bucket, default root object index.html, SPA error-response rewrite to index.html; (e) BucketDeployment of packages/frontend/dist with CloudFront invalidation; (f) CfnOutputs for ApiUrl, CloudFrontUrl, BucketName.

Ensure the frontend build gets its VITE_API_BASE_URL: document the two-pass approach in README (deploy API first OR use a known custom-domain), OR implement a runtime config.json approach: have CDK write a config file / or instruct building frontend with the API URL. Pick the simplest robust approach and document it clearly in README (prefer: deploy stack once to get ApiUrl output, set VITE_API_BASE_URL, rebuild frontend, deploy again; OR serve a /config.json from the bucket written by BucketDeployment with the API URL and have frontend fetch it at runtime). Implement the runtime config.json fetch in frontend api.ts if feasible so a single deploy works.

Update root README.md with: project overview (Japanese OK), architecture diagram text, growth stages + Bedrock model mapping table, prerequisites (Node >=18, AWS CLI configured creds, enable Amazon Bedrock Claude Haiku/Sonnet/Opus model access in the target region via the Bedrock console, region notes e.g. us-east-1), exact commands: npm install; npm run build; cd infra && npx cdk bootstrap && npx cdk deploy; how to get the CloudFront URL from outputs; how to override Bedrock model IDs via env (BEDROCK_MODEL_HAIKU/SONNET/OPUS) and default model IDs; local dev instructions (npm run dev in frontend, pointing VITE_API_BASE_URL at the deployed API); teardown (cdk destroy); and a clear note that this sandbox could not run npm install / cdk synth due to network restrictions so the user must run the build/synth/deploy locally.
Create a root .env.example documenting BEDROCK_MODEL_* overrides, AWS_REGION, ALLOWED_ORIGIN.
acceptance_criteria: CDK stack defines DynamoDB table, 4 Lambdas, HTTP API with the 4 routes + CORS, Bedrock InvokeModel IAM grant, and S3+CloudFront with BucketDeployment
chat/battle lambdas are granted bedrock:InvokeModel; getMonster/saveMonster are not required to have Bedrock perms
A single documented deploy path produces a working app (either runtime config.json or documented two-pass build) and README states it explicitly
README contains full prerequisites including Bedrock model-access enablement and default Claude model IDs, exact deploy commands, and the sandbox limitation note
All JSON config files (package.json, cdk.json, tsconfig.json, .env.example) are valid; TypeScript CDK files have no syntax (TS1xxx) errors under tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck
verification: env -u NODE_OPTIONS tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck --moduleResolution bundler --target ES2022 infra/lib/*.ts infra/bin/*.ts 2>&1 | (! grep -iE 'error TS1[0-9]{3}')
python3 -c "import json,glob,sys; [json.load(open(f)) for f in glob.glob('infra/**/*.json', recursive=True) if 'node_modules' not in f and 'cdk.out' not in f]; print('json ok')"
Confirm README.md documents: prerequisites, Bedrock model access, exact cdk bootstrap+deploy commands, model ID overrides, and the sandbox-could-not-synth note (grep for key headings)
findings:
FEAT-004 complete. Created infra/ CDK v2 app + root README.md + root .env.example.

FILES:
- infra/package.json (@ddm/infra; deps aws-cdk-lib ^2.150.0, constructs ^10.3.0; devDeps aws-cdk ^2.150.0, @types/node ^20, ts-node ^10.9.2, typescript ^5.5; scripts build/synth/deploy/bootstrap/destroy).
- infra/cdk.json: app='npx ts-node --prefer-ts-exts bin/app.ts', context.allowedOrigin='*' + standard CDK feature flags.
- infra/tsconfig.json: standalone CommonJS/Node, target ES2020, strict, esModuleInterop, skipLibCheck, types [node]. Does NOT extend the shared tsconfig.base (no ts-import-rewriting), so CDK + ts-node behave normally.
- infra/bin/app.ts: new App(); reads allowedOrigin + bedrockModel* from context then env; env.account/region from CDK_DEFAULT_*.
- infra/lib/digital-monster-stack.ts: full stack.

STACK DETAILS:
- DynamoDB Table 'MonstersTable' (tableName=`${id}-Monsters`), PK id STRING, PAY_PER_REQUEST, removalPolicy DESTROY.
- 4 NodejsFunction lambdas (NODEJS_20_X, ARM_64) entry=packages/backend/src/handlers/{getMonster,saveMonster,chat,battle}.ts, handler='handler'. bundling: externalModules ['@aws-sdk/*'], minify, sourceMap, target node20. @ddm/shared resolved via workspace symlink by esbuild. commonEnvironment TABLE_NAME + ALLOWED_ORIGIN; chat additionally gets BEDROCK_MODEL_* only when provided, timeout 30s, memory 512 (others 10s/256).
- IAM: table.grantReadWriteData(getMonster, battle); grantWriteData(saveMonster); grantReadData(chat). chat.addToRolePolicy bedrock:InvokeModel on the three Claude foundation-model ARNs (arn:<partition>:bedrock:<region>::foundation-model/<modelId>), region via Stack.of(this).region, honoring overrides.
- HTTP API (aws-cdk-lib/aws-apigatewayv2 HttpApi + aws-cdk-lib/aws-apigatewayv2-integrations HttpLambdaIntegration, both STABLE in 2.150 - no alpha module needed). corsPreflight allowOrigins ['*'], allowMethods GET/POST/OPTIONS, allowHeaders ['*']. Routes: GET /monster/{monsterId}->getMonster, POST /monster->saveMonster, POST /chat->chat, POST /battle->battle.
- S3 bucket private (BLOCK_ALL, S3_MANAGED, enforceSSL), removalPolicy DESTROY + autoDeleteObjects. CloudFront Distribution with origins.S3BucketOrigin.withOriginAccessControl (OAC), defaultRootObject index.html, REDIRECT_TO_HTTPS, CACHING_OPTIMIZED, errorResponses 403/404 -> /index.html (200) for SPA.
- BucketDeployment: Source.asset(packages/frontend/dist) + Source.jsonData('config.json', { apiBaseUrl: httpApi.apiEndpoint }); distribution + distributionPaths ['/*']. SINGLE deploy wires frontend->API because frontend/src/config.ts fetches /config.json at runtime (field name apiBaseUrl confirmed). dist must exist at synth (README instructs npm run build first).
- CfnOutputs: ApiUrl, CloudFrontUrl (https://<distributionDomainName>), BucketName, TableName.
